segments.text: Madam Speaker, I move to consider the proposed budget of the Commission on Human Rights.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: Is there any objection? The Chair hears none. The motion is approved. Majority Leader.

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Madam Speaker, may we acknowledge the heads and officials of the Commission on Human Rights, namely the Chairperson, Attorney Richard P. Palpal-latoc, Commissioners Attorney Beda A. Epres,

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Attorney Faydah M. Dumarpa, Justice Monina A. Zenarosa, Judge Maria Amifaith S. Fider-Reyes, together with Executive Director Attorney Jacqueline Ann C. de Guia and Human Rights Violations Victims' Memorial Commission Acting Executive Director Lawrence Charles E. Salazar.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: We acknowledge the presence of the heads and staff of the Commission on Human Rights. Welcome to the House of Representatives. Majority Leader.

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I move that we open the period of sponsorship and debate, and I move to recognize the sponsor, Vice Chair Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez of Alona Partylist.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: Is there any objection? The Chair hears none. The period of sponsorship and debate is now open, and we recognize the sponsor

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: The budget of the Commission on Human Rights, in the person of Vice Chairperson of Appropriations Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez of Alona Partylist. You may now proceed.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, distinguished colleagues in the House of Representatives, magandang gabi po sa ating lahat. I rise today to sponsor the fiscal year 2027 budget of the Commission on Human Rights, an independent constitutional institution trusted with protecting the dignity and fundamental rights of every Filipino.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, allow me to put the CHR budget in perspective through one figure: 0.02%. Out of proposed 7.2 trillion national budget, only PHP 1.273 billion, or around 0.02%, is provided for the CHR under the National Expenditure Program. The Commission proposed 2.749 billion.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Even if Congress were to provide the entire amount, it would only represent around 0.04% of the national budget, from 0.02% to 0.04%. Napakaliit po ng hinihingi ng CHR, but it can make a meaningful difference in its ability to investigate human rights violations, assist victims, prevent abuse, and protect the rights of our people.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: We cannot continue asking the CHR to do more without giving it the resources necessary to fulfill its constitutional mandate. The CHR is not an adversary of government. Kakampi po natin ang CHR sa mabuting pamamahala. A stronger and independent CHR strengthens accountability, protects the vulnerable, and helps build public trust in our institution. Madam Speaker,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: 0.1% is a modest investment for our institution mandated to safeguard the rights of 100% of our Filipino people. For this reason, I respectfully urge this august chamber to support the approval and augmentation of the fiscal 2027 budget of the Commission on Human Rights. Maraming salamat po, Madam Speaker, and I am now ready to take questions from our distinguished

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I move that we recognize the Honorable Iris Marie de Mesa Montes of 4K Partylist to interpellate on the proposed budget.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: Representative Iris Marie de Mesa Montes of 4K Partylist is now recognized for her interpolation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Thank you Madam Speaker, Distinguished Sponsor, the Commission on Human Rights Family. Magandang gabi po sa inyong lahat.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Unang katanungan ko po, would the Commission agree that the credibility of the Philippines' human rights institutions is itself an important component of the country's credibility in the international community?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Thank you Madam Sponsor, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: The recent failure of our country's bid for a non-permanent seat in the United Nations Security Council,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: the Asia-Pacific contest to Kyrgyzstan in June 2026 has been interpreted by some as a human rights warning.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: In fact, prominent international human rights organizations including the International Coalition for Human Rights in the Philippines

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: have publicly interpreted this electoral setback as a direct reflection of ongoing concerns regarding our domestic human rights record,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Does the Sponsor share this view?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: What role exactly did this unresolved human rights violation, especially in the past administration, play in this outcome?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: one of the Commission's significant accomplishments has been the implementation of the Task Force on Zero Backlog Cases,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: which substantially reduced the number of pending cases and helped clean up and reconcile our case data.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: the Commission has identified 493 cases for reinvestigation in 2024,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: and the Task Force has directed of 289 cases reinvestigated in 2025.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Of these 289 reinvestigated cases, 140 cases are currently for disposition by the TF.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: The Task Force also successfully reviewed and evaluated these cases identified for reinvestigation,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: and has begun drafting the corresponding resolution for disposition.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: This process remains ongoing, with the Commission committed to completing the disposition of these cases by the end of the year, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair, Distinguished Sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Yung mga binanggit niyo po ay mga accomplishments po ba yan ng CHR?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: But I was actually trying to find out if, when I asked a while ago,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: if the Human Rights Record of the Philippines, as seen by the international community,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: had something to do with our lost bid to the UNSC,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: and to which you said in the affirmative,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: ang gusto ko pong malaman nga,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: ano po itong mga unresolved cases in the past administration that you think ay nakakapag-contribute doon sa paningin na iyon ng international community?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: for example po, ang ating pong mga naka-accomplish po ay katulad po ng red tagging and EJA.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Okay, thank you, Madam Speaker, Distinguished Colleagues.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Yung mga ganyan po, nabanggit niyo po yung mga red tagging EJK,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Whether these concerns ng international community, consistent po ba yan sa findings ng Human Rights Commission?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Po, ano po yung iniisip ng international community?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Yan din po ba ang paningin ng CHR?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Can CHR identify programs, especially in the 2027 budget

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: that have demonstrated measurable improvements in compliance with human rights standards?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Ano po yung mga programang nakapaloob dyan sa 2027 budget natin na magpapakita o magpapatunay na meron nga from the past administration, meron po tayong improvement ngayon?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: A human rights-centered national protection response mechanism.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: early warning, victim supports, and rapid response mechanism.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So, meron po tayo ng mga tinatawag po nating programa, katulad po ng Bantay Karapatang Pantao,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: which detect, monitor, and prevent human rights risks through data and intelligence.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Kalinga Karapatang Pantao provides holistic, victim-centered support, protection, and recovery services.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: At syempre po, meron din po tayong Tugon Karapatang Pantao, which responds quickly, coordinates,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: intervention, and ensure protection and accountability.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Maraming salamat, Madam Speaker, Distinguished Sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Let me move on to my next question.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Just this morning, during the budget deliberations of the Dangerous Drugs Board,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: the Sponsor, Congressman Marcy Cudoro, made mention of the necessity to include the Commission on Human Rights

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: as a part of the Board of the Dangerous Drugs Board.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: If ever we include the CHR in the DDB, of course, by way of an amendment to the law creating the DDB,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: how do you envision your role in shaping drug-related policy?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Chair, alam niyo po, mandato po ng CHR, lahat po ng karapatang pantao ay lagi po natin ang gagampanan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Pero doon po sa, kanina po sa Dangerous Drugs Board,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: siyempre po, more than willing po na makisama, makisuporta ang CHR,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: at magkaroon po kami ng sarili natin position paper sa lahat po ng mga cases na drug-related po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Actually, Madam Chair, Madam Speaker, Distinguished Sponsor,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: what the DDB, what the sponsor of the DDB budget really wanted was to include the CHR

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: in the board as to help in formulating policies, kasi policymaking po yung Dangerous Drugs Board,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: to help in the formulation of policies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: So, alam po natin naging issue yung mga EJK, mga drugs in the past.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: So, I think it really is necessary to include the CHR there.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: So, halimbawa po, kasi I'm looking at, I'm willing to sponsor a bill tungkol po dyan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: I'm looking at, for instance, in strengthening oversight sa human rights in drugs enforcement strategies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Ano ang pwedeng maitulong ng CHR in that regard?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Okay. Sagutin ko po muna yung unang question nyo po ulit, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: The DDB, no. The DDB has not included.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: The DDB has not engaged with CHR, but the CHR is more willing to be an observer po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: With regards po sa drug-related po, CHR proposes that drug use to be treated as a public health issue.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Kasi po, drug use is currently being over-criminalized where users who need services to address their dependence or use are instead treated as criminals and jails.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Drug cases contribute to more than 70% of the jails.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So, sa lahat po ng mga pinupuntahan po ng CHR, Madam Chair, 70% po ang mga nakakulong po sa ating mga PDLs po natin.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Yeah. What you said was as observer. Is that correct? Did I hear you right?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Hindi po, hindi po sang-ayon na maging permanent seat sa board yung CHR.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Kasi kung ang pagbabasehan po natin,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: nung kung nga po una, kung naka-apekto yung mga EJK, mga problema ng human rights violations doon sa drugs,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: hindi po ba dapat nandodon din ang CHR?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Kasi kung may mga usapin po tayo ng paglabag ng human rights doon sa mga biktima ng mga EJKs.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Chair, ulitin po namin, we cannot because we have to maintain our independence po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Ibig sabihin po, kung sakasakali, your participation would only be limited to being an observer

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: and not contributing to the policies of the Dangerous Drugs Board.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: We can contribute po. We can contribute po, Madam Chair, but we cannot sit as a regular member of the board, as an independent body.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So, yan po yung mandato sa atin ng konstitusyon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Opo. Naiintindihan po natin yun, pero parte po din ng trabaho.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Human rights ng CHR ang pagprotekta sa mga vulnerable grupo, katulad ng mga kabataan,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: and especially women, because the CHR has a gender—is the gender ombud.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Now, these people, yung mga youth, yung mga women, sila usually ang nabibiktima.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Ang karapatan nila ay nayuyurakan, natatapakan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: So, tungkulin ng CHR, then na maprotektahan sila.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: So, how do we reconcile now this mandate and this duty?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: If you are saying na hindi yan mandato po ng CHR?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Chair, kung Montes, I'm with you sa karapatan po ng lahat ng ating mga vulnerable sectors,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: but syempre po, CHR is not a part of the executive, but we can monitor and we are the advisor of the government.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Okay, thank you so much, Madam Chair, distinguished sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Ang sa akin lang po, it's also a matter of...

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: you know, balancing security and rights in policymaking.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: If the CHR does not see it that way,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: then perhaps there are other ways for which CHR can be able to contribute to policies

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: that affect human rights in the issue of drugs.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: CHR seats as observed in all interagency bodies,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: but it is also an activity...

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: It is also an activity for which CHR can participate in awarding recommendations to different agencies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: If that being so, Mr. Chair, kung nakaupo pala talaga doon,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: ano po ang naging contribution ng CHR noong mga panahon na may mga aligasyon ng paglabag ng karapatang pantao

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: sa mga tokhang, sa mga EJ case, and all,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: na naging sanhi kung bakit napasama yung ating iman,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: We are having our undertaking its own investigations.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So lahat po ng cases na nagkakaroon po tayo being forwarded po sa CHR,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: unang-una po tinatanggap po natin yan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: at syempre po, hanggang doon lamang po ang ating mandato,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Pero we can endorse, recommend sa mga different agencies po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Okay. Maraming salamat po, Madam Chair, distinguished sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: I was just exploring the possibility based on the pronouncements of Congressman Teodoro

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: during the budget deliberation this morning.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: So let me move on to another topic.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: I would like to emphasize that it provides free information, education, and campaign or IEC materials

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: to individuals and organizations to promote human rights,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: particularly among vulnerable, marginalized, and disadvantaged sectors.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: May I ask the CHR, does the Commission specifically maintain IEC materials

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: on the protection of women and violence, discrimination, harassment,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: and other violations of human rights?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: IEC materials information sa ating pong komisyon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Opo. Itong mga materials na ito, where do they exist?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: O are they distributed in far flung barangays, digital materials po lang ito?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Because sa pagkakaalam ko po, parang online na, no?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So, both physical and online po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: How do we distribute it so that...

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Actually po, meron pong mga visitations sa various organizations,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: sa ating pong mga barangays, municipality,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: na umiikot po ang ating pong komisyon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: How much po of your 2027 budget is allocated for the production,

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: printing, and dissemination of these materials?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, it's P94,643,000 ang aming proposed for 2027.

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Out of the P94,000,000, magkano ang halaga specifically targeting women?

segments.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Demesa Montes
segments.text: Out of the P94,000,000, ilan po doon ang halagang specifically nakatarget sa production of materials for women po?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Naka-lump sum po siya, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: At sa CHR, dapat ay naging malinaw kung saan dadalhin din ang pondong.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, bigyan ko lang po kayo ng ilang datos para po sa mga nire-request po natin sa unfunded laws.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: For example po sa ating special laws, yung pong RA-9851, International Humanitarian Law of 2009.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So nire-request po namin ito ng 15 million.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004, 6 million.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: RA-11188, Special Protection of Children in Situation of Armed Conflict Act, 350,000.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So ito po ay 3 years na po hanggang ngayon po ay hindi po nabibigyan ng budget.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: Kaya po siguro maganda rin makita sa inyong milestone, identification sa inyong 10-year program.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: Saan po natin, paano po natin sasabihin na marami?

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: Siguro din po, hindi naman po din tayo hihintulang sa pagkasabing dahil hindi siya napupondohan,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: ay wala na rin tayong gagawin about it.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: So, baka lang po, Madam Sponsor, baka humingi po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: Kasi ang marami po sa tanong na ito, ang pinakamahalagang mga tanong na ito,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: ay nagagaling din po sa mga kasamahan natin sa civil society organizations na nagtataka.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: At nagtatanong kung saan pumupunta yung accomplishments ng commission sa pag-realize ng targets niya para sa mga pagtapos ng kanilang termino bilang member ng NBank.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: So, baka po pwede din ako magtanong kailan ko po makikita yung dokumentong yun para po malaman natin at maibalik din natin sa mga samahan na ito na,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: ito po ang pwede natin i-review at tingnan para pakita natin yung supportang maaari natin ibigay sa CHR.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, we will provide po necessary documents. Magsasubmit po kami sa inyo.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Sabi po ng komisyon, sabi po ng ating chairman Richard Pagpalatok, kahit hanggang bukas daw po ay magproprovide daw po kami ng data sa inyo.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlene "Kaka" J. Bag-ao
segments.text: Abagahan ko yun na Madam Sponsor. Maraming po salamat. Yun lang po sa ngayon ang gusto kong maipahatid. Thank you so much Madam Speaker at sa lahat po na bubuo ng komisyon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I move to recognize Representative Sarah Jane Elago of Gabriela Women's Party List to interpellate on the proposed budget.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: Representative Sarah Jane Elago of Gabriela Women's Party List is hereby recognized for her interpellation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Tungkol sa nailabas na ulat ng Commission on Human Rights nitong April 7, tungkol sa panawagan ng dagliang aksyon para tugunan ang mga kondisyon at mga gaps para sa child protection sa ilang bahay pag-asa,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: sa buong bansa. Ito po yung ating mga facilities na magtitiyak sana na may rehabilitative, may digtas na espasyo para sa mga CICL na matugunan yung pangangailangan para ho sila ay makabalik muli sa ating society, makapagpatuloy ng pag-aaral at matiyak ang karapatan ng mga bata.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ang ilan sa mga na-document na seryosong issues ng CHR ay tungkol sa mga gaps sa implementation ng Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Nandito rin po ang violence during a child's apprehension, ill-treatment by facility personnel, and facilities that are designed more like jails than safe spaces for children.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, nakikita rin po ang ganitong sitwasyon sa nailabas na report.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: ng Children's Legal Rights and Development Center tungkol naman sa mga torture cases at abuso sa mga bata, sa mga bahay pag-asa, ganon din po sa iba't ibang mga facilities sa buong bansa.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ang tanong po natin para sa Commission on Human Rights, mula po ma-issue ninyo ang ulat na ito, naglabas din po kayo ng detalyado na situation report, meron na po bang tugon ang mga relevant agencies kung paano matitiyak na may aksyon?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, meron po tayong datos sa katanungan po ni...

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Last Tuesday po, we presented sa isang forum lahat po ng mga government agencies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Ito pong inyong mga tinanong ngayon, Kong Ilago.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, bukod sa ating pinakahuli na situation report, meron din tayong updated na data at information tungkol sa kalagayan ng ating bahay pag-asa facilities.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Meron na ba tayong coordination? Present din po ba sa inyong ginanap na forum, halimbawa ang DSWD, para investigahan ang ganitong mga kaso?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, yes po. Bukod po sa DSWD, nandoon din po ang PNP, ang DILG at AFP po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, meron ding mahalagang center ang CHR tungkol sa pagtataguyod ng karapatan ng mga bata, ang Child Rights Center.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Sa ngayon po ba, magkano po ang nakalaan na pondo para sa Child Rights Center?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, muli at tulad po ng ating paninindigan noong budget briefing, ang mga policy center na ito ay susi para matiyak natin na ang ating mga aksyon, mga desisyon, mga posisyon sa iba't ibang issue,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: lalong-lalo na sa paggamit ng pondo ng ating bayan, ay nagagabayan ng datos.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At ang sinasabi ngayon, Madam Speaker, nangangailangan na tugunan natin agad itong nakakaalalaan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Mga kaso ng torture at child protection gaps sa ating bahay pag-asa facilities.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Naka-lump sum po siya sa ating

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: policy program para po sa formulation and advocacy of human rights

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Plans and Programs and Monitoring Implementation of International Human Rights, nagkakahalaga po siya ng 79 million pesos.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Alam ko ho na malayo pa iyan doon sa mga kinakailangan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Hindi lang po hinihiling pero pinapanawagan ng ating mga policy centers para sa sapat na pondo para mapagpatuloy ang kanilang mahalagang trabaho.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ngayon naman, Madam Speaker, tungkol sa Human Rights Violations Victim Memorial Commission.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Base po sa General Appropriations Bill na ating tinatalakay ngayon,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: bumaba ang budget ng Human Rights Violations Victim Memorial Commission mula sa 62,504,000, naging 61,174,000 na lamang.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ano po ang dahilan ng pagbaba nito?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At sa ngayon po, maari ba tayong bigyan ng update?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ano na ang status ng pagtatayo o yung pagtatayo ng mga dapat matapos ng komisyon na ito?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, kasi po ang ating capital outlay po ngayon ay zero ang allocation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So compared po last year, kahit po paano, meron po tayong capital outlay.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, hingin na rin po natin muli yung detalye tungkol dito at maisumite sa representasyon na ito mula sa kababaihan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ngayon naman po tungkol sa naiulat na nawawala na trust fund ng mga PDL sa CIW, sa Correctional Institute for Women.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At dito po, naiulat din sa kapulungan na ito na may aabot sa 60%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At ang tindig dito ng CHR ay dapat magkaroon ng independent probe sa nawawalang CIW-PDL trust fund.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Maari ba tayong bigyan ng update tungkol sa nasabing independent investigation?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At paano matitiyak din ang Kongreso na magagamit nito ang kanyang kapangyarihan sa oversight para matiyak na magagawa ng CHR ang kanyang trabaho?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Na kung meron mang dapat silipin, dapat gawin o mabago para mapagtibay ang palisiya para magawa ang independent probe, ay magawa natin ito.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, until now ongoing po ang investigation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: PDLs raise allegations regarding irregularities in the handling, accounting, and release of funds under the CIW-PDL trust fund,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, sinusuportahan ng representasyon na ito ng kababaihan ang paglulunsad ng independent probe ng Commission on Human Rights sa nasabing issue.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Hindi biro ang abot sa 6 million pesos na nawawala.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Dapat may malinaw na mapanagot tungkol dito.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Habang tinitiyak din natin na yung capacity ng CHR na magsagawa ng ganitong mga independent probe, magawa nila ng nasa oras.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Hindi lang po ito tungkol sa pananagutan, sa accountability, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Sa tingin po natin, dapat meron ding malinaw na direksyon paano ba mababalik yung mga nawawalang mga pondo na yan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At paano natin matitiyak na hindi na mauulit ito muli sa ating mga facilities.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ngayon naman, Madam Speaker, nais ko rin pong magtanong isang bagay na ibahagi ko rin kanina sa harap ng issue.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Tungkol po ito sa issue ng mga kababayan natin na magpasa hanggang ngayon,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: siyempre taon, matapos ang Marawi siege, ay nasa temporary shelter pa rin.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Nagkaroon po ba ang pag-aaral ang CHR? Nagkaroon po ba kayo ng pagbisita?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Nagkaroon na po ba ng mga pinakahuling pag-uulat na tungkol sa sitwasyon ng ating mga internally displaced persons?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At paano po natin napapaabot sa iba't ibang mga agencies ang kanilang mga pangangailangan para sa makataong kondisyon?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At matiyak yung kanilang karapatan na mabuhay ng may pantay na karapatan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, with regards po sa ating Marawi siege, I am with you, Kong Sara.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So, CHR granted financial assistance to 2,372 claimants, amounting to 7.1 million pesos.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: We have also issued a human rights advisory with continuous monitoring of compliance with laws and standards described in the advisory.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Meron din po tayong issuance of press statement

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: And sa totoo lang po, ngayon pong November, sabi po ng komisyon, sila po ay pupunta uli sa Marawi City.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Madam Speaker, sa pagpunta ng komisyon sa darating na Nobyembre dito sa Marawi, ano po ang particular na layunin ng pagbisita na ito?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Lalong-lalo na, meron hong bagong executive order tungkol sa pagtatatag ng Office of the Presidential Advisor for Marawi Rehabilitation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: And development na is po natin, kumbaga hindi lang po ito ginawa para lang masabi na meron tayong ganitong office.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Pero matiyak na ang office na ito na naitatag ay tutugon talaga sa agad na mga pangangailangan ng ating mga kababayan na ID,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: na hanggang ngayon ay nakakaranas pa rin ng nakakulangan sa adequate housing sa kanilang lugar.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Ang pagpunta po doon ng komisyon ay magkakaroon po tayo ng diagolo para po sa ating mga residente ng Marawi City.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: At syempre po, sa D-SUD po, nagpadala na rin po tayo ng letter para po i-raise yung operationalized MCB provided

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: at nagbigay po tayo ng recommendation and technical assistance para sa kanilang sekretariat.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At nagpaabot po noon ng panawagan din ang mga residente sa Marawi sa pangunguna ng Marawi Advocacy Accompaniment

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: na magkaroon ng dialogo at konsultasyon na ispo sana namin natawagan din ang Center for Social Justice and Humanitarian Protection

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: para doon sa mga issues, concerns, at needs po nila ay maisama naman doon sa magiging plano

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Kumbaga, matiyak po natin na sa lahat ng mga magiging plano, kasama mismo yung tao.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, sa November 17 po, pupunta po ang komisyon sa Marawi at magkakaroon po tayo ng Multi-Stakeholder Forum on Housing,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Land Property Rights, at kasama din po rito ang Marawi Board.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At harap din sa kapulungan na ito ang...

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At marami din pong mga katanungan ng ating mga kababayan kung paano ba gagamitin at ginagamit ang pondo ng bayan

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: dahil ngayong 2027, sa susunod na taon, zero ang pondo nila para sa susunod na taon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ngayon, malinaw na marami pa rin mga nangangailangan, kaya dapat po natin itulak kasabay ng pagtataas ng pondo ng CHR,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: mga bodies na tumutugon sa pangailangan ng mga affected pa rin na stakeholders sa Marawi.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ngayon naman bilang panghuli, Madam Speaker, nais ko lang pong mapaalalahanan ang ating CHR tungkol sa ating request.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Kung meron na kayong assessment sa role ng CHR sa pagtitiyak ng right to adequate housing at right against unjust demolition,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: kung meron na po kayong ulat tungkol dyan, dahil kayo po ay kasama sa dapat sa mga panahon na magkakaroon ng mga demolisyon

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: at maobserba na naoobserba natin yung mga protocols, yung mga policies na nagtataguyod sa karapatang pantao, number one po yan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At number two, kung sa tingin po ba ninyo ay kailangan pa natin ang mas pangil at mas malakas po,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: yung mga kapangyarihan para matiyak talaga na mauuna ang karapatang pantao sa pagtataguyod ng karapatan sa sapat at disente na panirahan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, may commission and bank na po tayo, may commission and bank resolution na po tayong naibigay dito,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: at ang commission po ay kasama pa rin po sa pre-demolition board.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At yan po ang hihintayin ng ating representasyon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Magiging resulta ng pagpupulong na yan at kung may kopya na kayo ng resolution.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: At ang hiningi nga po natin yung evaluation ng gaps eh, kung meron.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Kasi meron din sa ating kongreso, Madam Speaker, matagal nang sinusulong ng CHR yung pagpapalakas sa ating National Human Rights Institution.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ilang kongreso na rin niyang sinusulong dito sa House of Representatives.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: May nakapasa dito pero nabibinbinbin sa Senado o kaya po talagang hindi nakakaabot ang pagpasa.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Kaya ang hamon sa ating 28th Congress, hindi lang matiyak ang sapat na pondo sa CHR, kundi mapasa na rin ang mga mahalagang batas na ito,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: ang strengthening ng CHR bilang National Human Rights Institution, kasama na rin po ng protection ng rights ng human rights defenders.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Meron din po tayo ngayong nakakaabot.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Ang bang na panukalang batas para sa National Preventive Mechanism para matiyak na compliance sa optional protocol sa Convention Against Torture ang ating mga batas, ang ating mga palisya.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Kaya naman, Madam Chair, dito na po ako magtatapos.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Hindi pa rin po nagbibigay ang CHR ng ulat tungkol dun sa hinihain ng mga kababaihan mula sa Marikina.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Tungkol po sa ulat sa kanilang lugar ng presence po na nagbubunga o naghahatid po ng threat, harassment, at intimidation sa kanilang mga lugar.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Kaya po, yan na lang po ang maitutulak natin sa CHR na dagliang maipaabot sa representasyon na ito.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sarah Jane I. Elago
segments.text: Maraming salamat, Madam Speaker. Maraming salamat, Distinguished Sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I move that we recognize Representative

segments.speaker: Rep. Manuel "Wowo" L. Fortes Jr.
segments.text: Dadah Kiram Ismula of the Akbayan Party-list to interpellate on the proposed budget.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula of Akbayan Party-list is now recognized for her interpellation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: Magandang gabi po, Madam Speaker, Madam Sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: Madam Speaker, Madam Sponsor, meron lamang akong ilang katanungan related to the disposition of cases handled by the Commission.

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: Distinguished Sponsor, under the 2027 NEP ng CHR, can you describe what the Human Rights Protection Program is about?

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: And can the good sponsor also please describe how this program and its services can help an ordinary citizen, for example, a Moro or indigenous person? Thank you.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, the Human Rights Protection Service is the operational arm responsible for investigating complaints,

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: manages cases, and delivering direct intervention for victims of human rights violations.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: So, yung key functions and services po are independent investigations, quick response operations, legal aid and counseling, forensic and medical legal services, financial assistance, and witness protection.

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: Paano po kaya ito makakatulong sa isang ordinaryong mamamayan or ordinary citizen, for example, a moro or indigenous person?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Madam Speaker, yung ating mga clients, actually po, pwede po silang pumunta walk-in, physical in-person, o pwede rin po nilang bisitahin ang ating mga regional offices.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Meron po tayong 17 regional offices sa buong Pilipinas.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Pwede rin po silang mag-message sa FB.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Meron din po tayong online portal, yung tinatawag po natin mismo.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Meron din po tayong hotlines, emails.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Pwede rin po silang magbigay ng letters.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: At saka motu proprio, our own investigation and initiative.

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: So, Madam Sponsor, if an ordinary citizen wants to avail the services of this Human Rights Protection Program, ano ang process for them to avail?

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: Bukod doon sa nabanggit ninyong mag-walk-in, magsusulat, paano po kaya yung proseso nila?

segments.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
segments.text: Pagdating ko doon, paano po kaya yung magiging proseso?

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Wala po yung, ang komisyon po ay, wala po silang formal process na tinatawag.

segments.speaker: Rep. Ma. Cristina Talavera Lopez
segments.text: Formal complaint. Lahat po ay, pag pumunta po doon, yung po ay agad-agad nating tutugunan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Speaker. I happily address my colleagues here in plenary. I rise to sponsor the proposed fiscal year 2027 budget of the Department of Information and Communications Technology and its attached agencies. For fiscal year 2027, DICT and its attached agencies are proposing a total expenditure program of 19.49 billion pesos, an increase of 1.27 billion, or 7%, from fiscal year 2026.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: A significant portion of this budget goes to ICT infrastructure. The ICT Systems and Information Infrastructure Program receives 3.85 billion, as well as 1.13 billion for the National Broadband Plan, up by 69.3%, and 949.5 million for the National Government Data Center, up 27%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: These investments are already producing results. The National Fiber Backbone has laid 3,026 kilometers of fiber; 59 of 136 backbone nodes have been activated. And the Philippine Digital Infrastructure Project has an estimated cost of 16.1 billion, with 2.16 billion programmed for fiscal year 2027.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: For connectivity, DICT reported 29,091 active free Wi-Fi points across 11,839—sorry, I stand corrected—11,836 locations as of July 2026. The Free Public Internet Access Program has 5 billion pesos in automatic appropriations for fiscal year 2027.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Our digital government infrastructure is also operating at a significant scale. The eGov PH application has surpassed 61 million downloads

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and 56 million verified accounts, while eGov DX has

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: processed more than 1.2 billion transactions and integrated over 1,300 government e-services.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Cybersecurity, the National Security Operations Center, has expanded its coverage from 10 government agencies in 2022 to 99 agencies as of August 2026, monitoring approximately 6.7 billion security alerts.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But as we support these investments, we must also look closely at implementation. DICT's fiscal year 2025 obligation rate was 61.7%, leaving approximately 9.16 billion in unused appropriations.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: For the ICT Systems and Information Infrastructure Program, obligation was 43.5%. Disbursement was 22.6%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: These figures remind us that the measure of budget is not only what we appropriate, but what is actually delivered.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And while we recognize the progress made, we also recognize that there are many shortcomings still, not only in cybersecurity, but also in combating fake news and other areas of digital safety and governance.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: These are challenges that will require continued work and scrutiny.

segments.text: And while many may look at it as an opportunity to reduce funding for the agency, I see this as a challenge to increase funding where it is critically necessary.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: These programs are of the utmost importance for the development of our country in this new age of innovation, AI, cybersecurity, and other threats.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, Madam Speaker, with that, we are ready to take the questions of our distinguished colleagues, and I thank you.

segments.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith T. Flores
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I move that we recognize the Honorable Robert Nazal of BH Party-list to interpellate on the proposed budget.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez
segments.text: Representative Robert Nazal of BH Party-list is hereby recognized for his interpellation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Good evening to my distinguished colleague.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And good evening to the DICT.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: On the mandate of DICT, distinguished colleague, Mr. Sponsor, Madam Chair, I want to start with DICT's mandate.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: DICT is supposed to lead our national ICT agenda.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: we have an even bigger responsibility for whole of government digitalization and interoperability.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Madam Chair, distinguished colleague, Mr. Secretary, are you actually fulfilling that mandate?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Because DICT should be more than Wi-Fi and connectivity.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: You should also make sure that government uses technology efficiently.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: For example, are we oversubscribed in cloud services?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Do you know how much cloud capacity government is paying?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Paying for versus actual average and peak?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: What about internet services? Are we paying for more bandwidth than government actually uses?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: During our previous hearing, you told us Republic Act 12254 could save government at least 30% by eliminating repetitive common systems and subscriptions.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Have you already identified these duplications? How much can government actually save? And when will we see those savings?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Speaker. Those are very valid questions from my colleague. Let's go through it one by one very quickly.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So yes, Madam Speaker, DICT is implementing its mandate beyond the connectivity and moving towards a whole of government.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And that is currently being implemented through the DICT and its attached agencies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: For fiscal year 2027 alone, the department targets integration of 40 agencies with the Citizen Frontline Delivery Services Platform,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: 30 agencies, each of which with HCMIS and IFMIS, and 30 agencies with OFMIS.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And that includes the Online Public Service Portal and Procurement Systems.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Regarding the concern on cloud and bandwidth and other common ICT requirements,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: the objective of e-Government Act is precisely to give government greater visibility over what common requirements exist

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and to avoid paying repeatedly for the same capabilities.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So the management mechanism that we have here, and its ability to validate across

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: 450 national agencies for compliance, is established within the eGov portfolio.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But we should not complain or I mean we should not claim, sorry, rather, that DICT is oversubscribed in terms of its cloud or bandwidth

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: because the submissions presently available to DICT do not yet establish government-wide average and peak utilization

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: across or against total contracted capacity.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We can commit to Congress to establish that a baseline through the inventory, portfolio management,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and interoperability mechanisms are being implemented under RA 12254.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The 30% figure that my colleague brought up, Madam Speaker, is a very valid number to bring up

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: because we did make that commitment.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And the figure, therefore, should be treated at this stage as a potential cost avoidance estimate

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: ...common systems and subscriptions, not yet as realized savings.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So really, this is the target that we hope to hit.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And yes, as of the last committee hearing that we had, Madam Speaker,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: I do remember that the DICT is actively identifying where those duplications exist

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and we're progressively moving towards a consolidated system, common ICT investments,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So I believe that we're really targeting that by the end of this administration,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: we have a more centralized EGov system.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: I hope that answers my colleague's questions.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Thank you for that, Distinguished Sponsor, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Do we already have a number on the target in terms of the 30% savings that we will generate?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Do we already have a figure?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: How much has been saved already?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Let me get back to you on that.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, the DICT's claim is that they don't have a set number yet,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Is there a target number in terms of savings?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: For this year or for fiscal year 2027?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: But for this year, we'll allow it.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Because this is a new law, a newly passed law,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: the actual estimated savings are for fiscal year 2027,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: and we're looking at, if I'm not mistaken, 15 billion pesos in estimated savings

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Are we also looking at using AI to monitor all these systems?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, DICT can confirm that we are using AI.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Thank you for that, Distinguished Sponsor, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: I'll go to my next question.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Madam Chair, Madam Speaker, during the previous hearing,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Distinguished Sponsor, I also raised that the DICT has a 9% obligation rate.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: We are told now that this has improved to around 27%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Yes, Madam Speaker, I can confirm we've increased to 27%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, okay naman po na hindi na 9%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: 27% na, pero I hope we shouldn't be happy with this, no?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: May I ask, why, what is stopping us from improving on the 27%?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I completely agree with my colleague.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: especially when there are so many other agencies that need funding.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And I'll list down the things that are making it difficult.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Two is the technical complexity of what DICT's management,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: mandate, puts them in charge of.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Three is the timing of the release of funds.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Many of the releases were quite late this year for DICT.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And so, many of the funds are just now being released.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We also have a limited specialized manpower.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Unlike many other agencies, DICT requires a lot of specialized manpower, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And with that, we actually do need to increase the manpower of the agency

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: ...increase its absorptive capacity and the services it provides.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Lastly, PDIP had two unsuccessful biddings and had to restructure its major procurement package.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And all of that combined leads to 27%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: What obligation rate, Mr. Sponsor, are we looking at for December 31?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, the agency is optimistically pointing out that we're looking at 90% completion by December.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, are we saying that considering what you've mentioned, Madam Chair and Mr. Sponsor,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: maaayos na po natin yung procurement issues,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: we will have all the technical manpower prior to that?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: as of today, we're at 35% already.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And we are expecting how much? 90?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And if you think about it,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: when we had the initial data to today,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: If we continue at this rate,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: we could possibly hit our target of 90%.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: One of the things that the agency had to deal with

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: was really just waiting for the download of funding.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And so, there was time to already streamline some of the processes

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: for the release of these funds and the activation on the ground.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, what you're saying, Distinguished Sponsor, Madam Speaker,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: is that maayos na po tayo in terms of the procurement process

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: But our main problem right now is the DBM.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And how long, and kailan natin natatanggap yung pera?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The reason why is not necessarily DBM.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: It turns out it's because the awarding of major projects

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: will take place within this quarter.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, once those have been awarded already,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But that doesn't necessarily have anything to do with the DBM.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: When were these projects supposed to be procured?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: At the start of the year

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, PDIP, which constitutes 4 billion pesos, Madam Speaker,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: is a big chunk of it.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And the reason why it was delayed

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: was because earlier this year, dear colleague,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: they actually had a failed bidding.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, now it's proceeding, but it's proceeding in October.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, that's why the 4 billion will be released quite later.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: But this was a project procurement for 2026 or 2025?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Let me go to my next question.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: I also want to be fair to the agency.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Hindi lahat ng hindi nababayaran ay necessarily Absorptive Capacity problem.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: you had approximately 1.29 billion in accounts payable.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Of that, approximately 1.049 billion pertains to

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: valid and duly supported obligations from 2024 and 2025

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: that are already due and demandable.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: You also say additional NCA from DBM is needed to settle these obligations.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: is the problem now lack of cash authority from DBM

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: How much additional NCA do you need today to settle all valid, due, and demandable obligations?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Yes, I can confirm that there is a payable of 1.049 billion and this, actually, we do need an additional allocation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And these are considered as milestone payments, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: if these are already valid, duly supported, and due and demandable obligations,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: and DICT submits the complete requirements,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: ang assumption po natin dito is complete na yung requirements nito.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, Madam Speaker, I can confirm that all the requirements needed to request for additional funding for NCA from DBM

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: is complete and it's actually subject for approval already.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: What are they saying is the reason why hindi pa ito nababayaran?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: What is the reason for the delay?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Could you pause my time, please?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The documents were submitted first semester of this year—sorry, third quarter of this year, dear colleague.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So that probably explains why until now the release has not yet been approved.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So that's what I do not understand.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Bakit po inabot tayo ng third quarter of this year to complete the requirements for something that is due and demandable since 2024?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Why? Why wasn't it submitted? We already knew that this was going to be a project.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The reason why there was a delay in the submission of the necessary documents was they needed to compile the requirements from the suppliers, etc.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And they were only able to do so later this year.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, the delay is a mix of agency as well as suppliers.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: What I cannot understand is that the DICT should be the number one digital agency in our country.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Kayo po ang lead sa lahat.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, dapat po, kung meron man madi-delay, hindi po dapat kayo.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Dear colleague, I completely understand where you're coming from.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: If there's any agency that should move quickly on a digitalized procurement and documentation process, it should be the DICT.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, I believe I can get a commitment from the agency that they will improve their procurement processes.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Saka po, you know, distinguished sponsor, you know how easy it is now to review everything. We have AI.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: I know that the DICT is going to work towards better digitalization in terms of its bureaucracy.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Pero sana din pati yung suppliers ng DICT, dito tayo abot sa compatibility ng data.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, sana yung mga suppliers din ng DICT are up to standard in terms of their digitization para wala ng bottleneck.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: But of course, my understanding is that if you look at the way the DICT is paying,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: walang supplier na magsusurvive sa ganitong sitwasyon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, the suppliers are effectively front-loading everything.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, I understand that this disincentivizes some of our suppliers and potential investors

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: if this is how our lead digital agency deals with its documentation and disbursement processes.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, within this year, this outstanding balance should be settled by the DICT.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, if I may also note that 90% of cash downloaded by the DBM has already been utilized.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, it's really just a question of whether or not the funding is downloaded.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Once it is, it's immediately utilized by the agency.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, it's really a funding issue.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Yeah, I would say that a big chunk of it would be.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And I hope that this can be streamlined on the agency side.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, let us now go to earmarked funds.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: separate from the regular budget of DICT,

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: ng DICT when it comes to earmarked funds?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Lagi kasi namin kayong pinaglalaban because digitalization needs money.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And if we should be spending on anything, it should be, we should prioritize the digital infrastructure.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Pero kung may malaking problema, yung earmarked balance naman at hindi ninyo nagagastos, ano ba ang problema?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: In terms of the earmarked funds, Madam Speaker, we're talking about the free Wi-Fi.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And that's at 61% in terms of utilization.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, that speaks to the absorptive capacity of the agency to be able to utilize the earmarked funds.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And that is what I cannot reconcile, Distinguished Sponsor, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Twelve digital systems hosted on the E-Gov PH were temporarily disabled

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: because DICT could not pay for cloud server space.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: How long were the systems down?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: It went down because, Madam Speaker, dear colleague, we had a surge of 700% in terms of its use.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We weren't able to handle that much.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And therefore, the systems went down for a short period of time.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, it was only down for five hours on day one and six hours on day two.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But this is definitely because no one was able to predict a 700% surge in the use.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Paano po ba nangyari yung surge?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: I mean, during that day or the day before that or the month before, ilan na ba yung gumagamit?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, was it only on that day na talagang nagkaroon ng surge?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And the capacity could not absorb it?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Mr. Speaker, it turns out that the cloud services ended up running out of credits because of the overuse.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And that's how we ended up with that surge.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, that means, hindi po natin...

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: We didn't have enough cash or money allotted for the capacity.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We didn't have enough budget enough for the surge that basically no one within the agency predicted that there would be a 700% surge in the use.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And therefore, the cloud services that were contracted weren't enough.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: And therefore, we needed to procure more in order to adapt to the capacity required.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, that's where I'm puzzled, Distinguished Sponsor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Nag-down ang 12 government systems dahil kulang tayo sa pambayad sa cloud.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Meron po kayong pera na dapat kayo mismo ay may access doon at madali niyong magamit.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And this is for free Wi-Fi and for our cloud services.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Madam Speaker, regarding that concern, that's correct that there are earmarked funds.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, it's not included in the earmarked funds as part of the automatic use.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, for data, we're unable to use those earmarked funds in order to fund cloud data.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Are we expecting this to happen again?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Or do we have enough funds already and credits, so-called credits, to cover any surge in the future?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Do we have access to the earmarked funds para hindi na ito mangyari ulit?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So based on the eGov law, Madam Speaker, we do have enough funds to maintain.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But that doesn't necessarily mean that we are at optimal.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: If I'm not mistaken, the budget that we're being given for these cloud services...

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: I mean, for our data services is about 949 million.

segments.speaker: Deputy Speaker Janette L. Garin
segments.text: For the honorable Nazal, if he could kindly wind up.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But the reality is, we actually need additional funds for redundancies.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: We need additional funds for emergency systems, which we don't have currently.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: So, if you're wondering why there's a risk of it going down,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: it's partly because we're underfunding this specific program.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: But the law does provide for the bare minimum required.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, what is the funding actually needed for us to be able to support?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: The request is 1.8 billion, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: So, bakit pa po natin kunin ito sa USF?

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: Well, that's a very valid point that the USF could possibly be used,

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: or earmarked funds could possibly be used for cloud services.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: However, unfortunately, that is not within the purview of the agency to decide that.

segments.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
segments.text: I believe that is a call of the DBM, if I'm not mistaken, Madam Speaker.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Maybe due to lack of time, I just have to bring this up.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: During our previous hearing also, we already discussed that much of the government data is hosted abroad.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: And that DICT needs local availability zones or data centers.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Hindi ko na po ulitin yun.

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: Ang follow-up ko lang, kailan matatapos ang migration?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
segments.text: What percentage of critical government data and workloads will be locally hosted by end of November 26?

segments.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal
